messages:
amal: Heads-up — since the 2.1.4 BMC firmware push to eu-west provisioning pool we've seen higher than usual serial console latency and a pile-up in the provisioner queue. Not full failure, but console IO stalls for ~10-25s on some nodes.
jia: saw similar on a couple nodes in eu-west-2 can repro with `screen /dev/ttyUSB0 115200` — you'll see long pauses mid-boot. Any correlation with NTP or watchdog changes in 2.1.4?
lucas: Firmware changelog mentioned 'NTP client refactor + reduced syslog batching' — could be related. Ops-bot shows a cluster-level jump in syslog forward/back timestamps around the deploy window.
amal: exact symptom: serial stream halts then resumes with a burst of buffered logs. Provisioner times out on console handshake and retries, doubling provisioning time.
jia: quick check: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U admin mc info` returns different uptime vs host uptime on affected boxes — suggests BMC clock drifting.
sre-oncall: Oncall here. Throttling new provisioning for eu-west pool and marking canary nodes out of rotation. Rolling back to 2.1.3 on a small canary recovered normal serial behavior.
lucas: thanks. Can you paste the rollback command you used? Want to script revert for remaining canaries.
sre-oncall: used vendor tool: `vendor-fwctl --host <bmc> --image fw-2.1.3.bin --force-reboot` and then `sleep 60 && ipmitool ... mc info` to wait for BMC to come back. Added a small loop to verify serial output resumes.
amal: good call. Also observed NTP offset spikes of up to 120s in BMC logs. That explains buffered syslog bursts when it corrects. We'll add an NTP hold tolerance to the runbook.
jia: temp mitigation idea: before big provisioning waves, run `ntpdate -u pool.ntp.org` on BMCs via ipmi if vendor supports it. For nodes without that, insert a 20s pre-provision sleep to avoid handshake timeouts.
lucas: long-term we should file with vendor; 2.1.4 probably introduced aggressive clock step behavior + serial buffer threshold bug. I'll open a ticket and attach capture.
amal: opened vendor ticket VND-4872 and attached `ttygrab` logs. Also starting a job to roll back non-critical canaries tonight.
sre-oncall: we pushed rollback to 10% of eu-west pool, provisioning latency dropped ~40% on those hosts. Keeping throttles active until vendor patch.
jia: noted. Adding a check to provisioning pipeline: if serial stall > 8s then mark BMC for rollback flag and prevent further attempts. Will PR in 10m.
lucas: also watch cost — longer provisioning increases transient GPU hours. Finance pinged earlier about a spike. Amal, can you estimate extra GPU-minutes from the last 6 hours?
amal: quick estimate: ~320 GPU-minutes across pending nodes (mostly from repeated retries). We'll produce a precise number in morning.
sre-oncall: thanks. For now: (1) throttle pool, (2) rollback canaries, (3) add pre-provision NTP/20s delay, (4) vendor ticket. I'll keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [automation] Started rollback job job_id=rb-20260319-euw-1 on 32 hosts — status: in_progress.
amal: closing loop — any objections to rolling back the rest of eu-west tonight if vendor ETA > 24h?
jia: +1 from infra. Prefer staged rollbacks to avoid unexpected side effects.
lucas: agree. Staged, monitor serial latency and provisioning queue.
sre-oncall: will coordinate schedule. Updating runbook with commands and thresholds now.
metadata_note: This thread documents an operational issue after a BMC firmware rollout causing serial console stalls and NTP skew, mitigations, rollback steps, and cost/coordination notes.
